answer.rationale: The competitive pressure makes promotional_pricing the emotionally obvious move, but memory_73 is the weakest record in the inheritance and the one most likely to mislead. It is written in compressed shorthand rather than the narrative form of the others, which suggests it has been through lossy consolidation; it reports signup +31% and rev +18% over a 12-week reporting window, which is short enough that it almost certainly measures acquisition rather than retained value. A 40% discount that lifts revenue 18% in-window can still be value-destroying once margin and the churn profile of price-sensitive acquirees are counted, and the note that 'segment def unchanged' hints someone previously worried about exactly that. So I want the original record for memory_73 to see the margin treatment and whether cohort retention was ever followed past the window. My second pull is memory_31, not because I doubt it but because it and memory_86 may not be independent evidence: 'cutting required fields at signup' and 'shortening onboarding' could be two consolidations of the same underlying experiment, in which case my apparent two-source support for onboarding work is really one source, and I should size accordingly. Absent verification I intend simplify_onboarding. It is the only direction that maps directly onto the two measured regressions (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) rather than papering over them with acquisition volume, and it compounds: accounts that reach first value are the substrate every other lever depends on. Referral incentive (memory_57) is credible but was validated on established customers and presupposes a healthy activated base that is currently eroding, so it is premature. Enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) is sound but addresses a segment that is not the one under attack and cannot be stood up meaningfully in one week. Discounting into a competitor's entry price also risks resetting SMB price expectations in a way that is hard to walk back, a cost that would not appear in any 12-week readout. Standard experiment scale with retention and margin instrumented as primary, not signup count; if memory_31 proves to be a duplicate of memory_86 I will drop to a small guarded test rather than assume the effect is doubly confirmed.
